extracted.intended_audience: amateur and professional observers/researchers of child language, genealogists, and educated popular-science readers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for recording and reporting single-case observational studies of infant language (phonetic records and behavioral interpretation), with related practical advice on genealogical record-keeping and cautious use of astronomical/geological evidence. Emphasizes notation, what to record, and how to treat uncertainty and comparative evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record only what is actually and distinctly observed
rubrics_metrics.description: I think I have set down nothing as fact which has not been actually and distinctly observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid speculation — report only directly observed utterances and behaviors. Distinguish observed facts from interpretation or conjecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not attempt exact dates unless comparing large samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Exact dates I have not attempted to give, conceiving that they would be of no use unless for the comparison of a very large number of observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For single-case or small-N observational reports, omit precise timestamps for each acquisition unless you plan statistical comparison across many subjects; dates are mainly useful for large-sample comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize order of acquisition rather than precise timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Children differ so much in forwardness that the time of particular acquisitions seems of little importance as compared with their order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When documenting development, report the sequence in which milestones/words/sounds appear; sequence is more informative than exact ages in single-case notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a consistent phonetic notation and explain it
rubrics_metrics.description: I thought it at least desirable to use some consistent notation for the sounds actually produced. For this purpose I have taken the Indian Government system, with a few additional signs which will speak for themselves. Words in italics are in the Indian Government spelling. Words between inverted commas are in ordinary English spelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare the phonetic system used, define special symbols and conventions (e.g., how unaccented 'a' is represented, use of italics vs. quotes), and stick to it throughout to allow others to interpret your transcriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide contextual interpretation of utterances and note ambiguity
rubrics_metrics.description: M-m generally indicated a want of something. Bd bd was: 1. A sort of general demonstrative, standing for the child herself, other people, or the cat ... 2. An interjection expressing satisfaction. Both sounds, however, seemed often to be made without distinct intention, as mere exercise of the vocal organs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record both the form of vocalizations and their observed contexts and possible functions; note when an utterance may be exploratory/practice rather than communicative intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep private family records in addition to official registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the establishment of a national system of registration of births, marriages, and deaths, there is not so much chance of the relationships of families being lost as there was ... it is a useful auxiliary to private registration, but cannot wholly supersede it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain family Bibles, private notes or registers alongside official records (national registration began in 1837 here); private records preserve details that may be hard to extract from indexes later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record dates and places of births/marriages/deaths to facilitate searches
rubrics_metrics.description: The date and place of either of the three occurrences in the life of a person with which genealogy especially concerns itself being known, it is easy to get an official record of the fact from the registrar-general; but to start with only a name, and to have to look through index after index to find the date ... is a very different matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assembling genealogical data, prioritize capturing date and place for the three vital events (birth, marriage, death) because these make retrieval from official indices straightforward; starting from a name alone is time-consuming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use parish/local registers and local sources to detect name localization
rubrics_metrics.description: The earliest documents in which names occur in any plenty, and from which we can judge of their distribution, are parish registers. In these we find that in each parish there is usually a marked preponderance of one name ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult parish registers and other local records to identify geographic clusters of surnames; national-level sources (e.g., Doomsday-Book) may be less useful for fine-grained localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be skeptical of ready-made pedigrees and claims of noble descent
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new man rises up ... his first conclusion is that he must necessarily be related to the best-known family of the name he happens to bear ... he probably applies to some professed pedigree-monger, who at once furnishes him with the missing links ... affixing ... the coat-of-arms ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demand documentary proof for claimed connections to prominent families; beware of forgers/pedigree-mongers and historical practices (e.g., alienation/assumption of arms or names) that can mislead surname-based inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin arguments with the items of greatest certainty; defer doubtful evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: I shall not introduce them for evidence in this stage of my inquiry, as items of the greatest certainty must claim the first attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure scientific argumentation by presenting the most secure, well-established evidence first; leave more speculative or uncertain items for later stages of the discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid false precision when data are uncertain; acknowledge vagueness
rubrics_metrics.description: In the vague use of this round number for marking the career of our globe, there is shown a wish rather to fix a limit to geological time than to adhere to strict mathematical precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When underlying measurements or inferences are uncertain, report ranges or acknowledge vagueness instead of presenting precise-seeming numbers that imply unwarranted accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparative planetary cases to bound or test hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: The neighboring zone of the solar system presents an actual case very similar to the extreme one under consideration. The difference between the equatorial and polar diameters of Mars is at least three times as great as that which could be expected from his present rotation ... it must be concluded ... about 800,000,000 years elapsed since the solidification took place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the phenomena observed on other planets (e.g., Mars' flattening, Saturn's rings) to test hypotheses about Earth's past and to provide bounds on timescales or processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine theoretical calculations, observational corrections, and literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Mayer was able to reproduce and to maintain on new grounds the almost forgotten doctrine of Kant. The evidence ... was subsequently strengthened by a discovery which Prof. Adams made, of an error in the investigations of Laplace; and soon afterward Delaunay ... found that the earth's diurnal motion is reduced on a scale corresponding to the waste of power involved in tidal movements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate theory, observation, and successive corrections to previous work; cite prior authorities, note corrections, and show how theoretical advances change interpretation of observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider long-term cumulative physical mechanisms (e.g., tidal friction) when inferring planetary changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the amount of energy thus wasted has been estimated as over two thousand times greater than that of the united labor of the entire human population, yet so great is the stock of working force embodied in terrestrial rotation that 20,000,000 years must elapse before the length of our day is increased one per cent, by tidal friction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for cumulative effects of slow processes (tidal friction, centrifugal changes) and perform energy/time-scale estimates to assess their geological or astronomical significance; quantify where possible to avoid qualitative misinterpretation.
